letter_markdown:
August 19, 2026

Aetna  
P.O. Box 14463  
Lexington, KY 40512  

Re: Expedited appeal of denial of lumbar decompression/discectomy  
Member: Morgan Lawson  
Member ID: W441316160  
Reference number: POC-CBB1679293-79812  
Requested procedure: CPT 63030  
Treating surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery  

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression/discectomy. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document substantially more than the required conservative-treatment trial.

The official Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin retrieved for spinal surgery is Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion, CPB 0743. The policy states:

“Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1* (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below);”

Morgan completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, from April 13, 2026, through July 6, 2026, with 16 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Morgan also used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on May 25, 2026, which provided only four weeks of partial relief. These records establish failure of an adequate conservative-treatment course.

The clinical record also supports the other lumbar-surgery criteria stated in the retrieved policy. The policy requires that:

“Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated;”

Morgan has radicular pain extending into the right calf, a positive provocative examination on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The policy further states:

“Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings;”

The June 23, 2026, lumbar MRI documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This imaging finding corresponds to Morgan’s right-sided radicular symptoms and neurologic deficit.

The policy also requires:

“Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;”

Morgan cannot stand for more than 10 minutes because of the symptoms. The lower-back pain has progressed over 18 months and remains unrelieved by rest.

The request is therefore supported by:

- 18 months of progressive lower-back pain;
- 12 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy;
- Eight months of NSAID treatment without adequate relief;
- Only four weeks of partial relief after the May 25, 2026, corticosteroid injection;
- MRI-confirmed L4-L5 disc extrusion and severe right lateral recess stenosis;
- Compression of the traversing L5 nerve root;
- Right-calf radicular pain;
- A corresponding neurologic deficit and positive provocative testing; and
- Significant functional limitation, including inability to stand longer than 10 minutes.

There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking. Morgan’s BMI is 29. The requested surgery is being recommended by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgeon, to decompress the affected neural elements after conservative treatment has failed.

Please overturn the denial and approve CPT 63030. If Aetna maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical criteria actually applied to this request, including the policy version and effective date, and explain specifically why the documented 12-week physical-therapy course, eight months of NSAID treatment, and corticosteroid injection were not considered an adequate conservative-treatment trial.

Please treat this as a pre-service medical-necessity appeal. If the clinical reviewer determines that a delay could worsen Morgan’s neurologic condition or prolong severe pain and functional loss, please process the appeal under the applicable expedited-review procedure.

Sincerely,

Morgan Lawson  
Member ID: W441316160  

Enclosures: Denial notice; physical therapy discharge note; medication and treatment history; corticosteroid-injection record; June 23, 2026, lumbar MRI report; orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation; other relevant medical records
